incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-5568 fired for service=canary-inference-us-west - 5xx error-rate spike (current 4.8%, threshold 3%)
jax: grabbing this — i'm primary oncall (jax). linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-failures
samira: acked. any obvious recent deploys?
matt: deploy to canary pool went out ~15m ago, tag=release/2026-03-14-41, rollout batch=5% -> 20%
lee: seeing similar error spike in logs: model loader OOMs, kube events show node pressure in canary GPUS
jax: pasting recent logs: ```2026-03-14T02:12:45Z inference-worker[pid=2145]: ERROR model_load: OOM while allocating KV cache; retrying...
2026-03-14T02:13:01Z proxy[info]: upstream 10.4.31.22: inference error: 502 bad gateway
```
matt: hmm that's the new quantized runtime change from the last PR. reverting sounds likely. we can scale canary cpu/gpu?
samira: customer-impact estimate? dashboards show increase in 5xx for two customer-facing endpoints — but overall traffic drop is small, about 1.2% of requests failing, concentrated in us-west-canary pool
pd-bot: PagerDuty PD-5568 acknowledged by jax at 02:20 UTC
jax: plan: 1) pause rollout traffic (stop ramp to next batch) 2) scale canary pool down for safety 3) rollback the runtime change in canary 4) monitor for 15m -> decide full rollback
lee: commands I'm running: `kubectl -n redwood set image deploy/inference-canary inference-worker=redwood/inference:release-2026-03-13-legacy` and `kubectl patch traffic-split canary --patch '{"spec":{"weights":{"canary":5}}}'`
matt: i'm pausing the rollout in the control plane now (console -> Rollouts -> pause). confirming API call successful.
onchalant-reaction: :eyes: (not a user message, annotation)
jax: rollback triggered, image set to release-2026-03-13-legacy on canary nodes. scaling down canary instances to 8 -> 4 while rollback finishes
samira: I'm messaging support ops to flag impacted customers and add proactive note in status page draft
matt: note: autoscaler did spin up 2 extra nodes right before spike; that might've mixed instance types with different CUDA drivers -> mismatch with our quantized kernels
lee: digging into node bootstrap logs, saw `driver mismatch: cudart 12.0 vs expected 11.8` on two nodes from pool-uswest-preemptible-2
jax: good catch. i'm draining those nodes permanently from canary pool: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`
pd-bot: PagerDuty PD-5568 escalated to SRE lead (samira) at 02:32 UTC because ack > 10m without resolution
samira: I'm on call lead, coordinating with release engineer (matt) and infra (lee). Can someone confirm if any customer-facing async jobs failed?
matt: some low-priority async retries logged but no durable data loss. retry queue backpressure visible but within tolerance.
jax: rollback completed at 02:38 UTC, healthchecks passing in canary: 2xx > 99% across probes. reverting traffic-split to baseline now.
lee: removed mismatched nodes from canary pool and filed infra ticket INF-9821 to prevent future driver drift
samira: good - start 15m observation window. If errors stay <0.5% we can resume rollout. Also, reach out to the release owner to audit the quantization runtime test matrix.
pd-bot: PagerDuty PD-5568 auto-resolved at 02:55 UTC after incident-bot healthcheck passed 3 consecutive checks
matt: rolling back rollout pause now? i'd like to keep it paused until release owner confirms driver compatibility fix.
jax: agreed. leaving rollout paused. i'm posting summary to #postmortems once we get the final timeline
samira: handoff: i'm logging this as an incident (INC-2026-03-14-07). oncall handover to night SRE (lee) at 03:00 UTC for watch window.
lee: got it. i'll keep monitoring dashboards and watch for regressions. please add any follow-ups to the incident thread.
samira: follow-ups: 1) pin runtime images to exact cuda driver in canary pools 2) expand canary node driver validation in CI 3) add rollback automation to pause rollout + revert image and traffic-split in one step
matt: filing followups now: RFC-1263 (runtime pinning), JOB-456 (driver validation), AUTO-77 (rollback automation)
jax: final check: error-rate back down to 0.3% in us-west canary, latency stable. closing this thread from oncall perspective. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Oncall handover to lee recorded at 03:00 UTC
lee: acknowledging handoff. I'll escalate immediately if any uptick. thanks team. :pray:
